Half a term's notice to leave, by message.

sections.title: Drop-off and collection
sections.body:
Please bring dancers to the foyer door no more than ten minutes before class, and collect them from the same door.

If someone else is collecting, message us before the class.

sections.title: Photographs and filming
sections.body:
We never post children's faces without written consent from a parent.

No filming in class; we film the shows and send them to parents.

sections.title: What to bring
sections.body: A named water bottle, and the uniform for the class. Long hair tied back.

sections.title: Illness
sections.body: If she's unwell, please keep her at home and message us; the class can be made up in the same week.

sections.title: Safeguarding
sections.body: Our safeguarding policy and the name of our safeguarding lead are on the noticeboard in the foyer. Ask us for a copy.

handbookPage.title: Everything *for the year.*
handbookPage.intro: Sample handbook for a fictional school.

showDay.text: On show week each class's code is in its WhatsApp group. Type it here for arrival time, stage door, costume, hair and collection.

photo.alt: A dancer rehearsing alone on a large empty stage, seen from behind

path.text: Usually, when her teacher says she's ready. Every dancer moves up in her own time; nobody is held back for an exam.

items.text: She was nervous at the door and didn't look back once. Three terms in, she still talks about the trial.
items.author: Hannah L.

items.text: The timetable and the term dates in my calendar: the first dance school that hasn't needed a spreadsheet.
items.author: Tom R.

items.text: Seeing him on a real stage at the winter showcase. We booked the summer show the same night.
items.author: Priya S.

questions.a: From two, with a grown-up beside her; on her own from three.
Yes: the first class is a trial. Pick the age above and message us.
Every class is open to everyone, and there's a boys' class on Saturdays.
Parents wait in the foyer. There's a watching week at the end of each term.

questions.q: What if we miss a class?
questions.a: Come to another at the same level in the same week, if there's room.

questions.q: My child has additional needs. Can she join?
questions.a: Please message us: we'll talk it through with you before the trial.

questions.q: Does everyone dance in the shows?
questions.a: Yes, every class from Little ballet up, twice a year.

steps: Leave by the main exit and turn left
Cross at the lights onto Coleby Walk
Linden Hall is the red-brick hall on the right
Follow the one-way system towards the station
Drop off at the hall gate; no parking on the walk

blocks.heading: What happens
blocks.body:
Ballet, a little jazz and a story danced from start to finish, shown to parents on the last morning.

Nine till twelve, with a snack break. Bring a packed snack and water.

blocks.body:
One of our teachers leads an hour of dance and games for up to fifteen children, aged three to eight.

At Linden Hall on a Saturday afternoon, or at your home.
